subject: french
promptStrong: Give me a 40-word writing task in French on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer for accuracy and range.
promptWeak: Give me a two-way translation drill (French↔English) on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, with answers and the common mistakes to avoid.

questions.q: How do you say 'I play football' (a sport)?
questions.explain: Sports take 'jouer à': 'Je joue au football'. Instruments take 'jouer de' (e.g. 'je joue du piano').

questions.q: How would you write 'sportif' to describe a sporty woman?
questions.explain: Adjectives ending in -if change to -ive in the feminine singular, so a sporty woman is 'sportive'.
« Tricoter » means to knit; « le tricot » is knitting.
'Le temps libre' means 'free time'. Note 'le temps' can also mean 'weather', but 'libre' (free) makes it 'free time' here.

questions.q: What does 'J'ai l'habitude de lire le soir' mean?
options: I would like to read in the evening
I usually read in the evening
I have to read in the evening
I used to read in the evening
questions.explain: 'Avoir l'habitude de' means 'to be in the habit of / usually do', so this is 'I usually read in the evening'.
False friend: 'sensible' in French means 'sensitive'. 'Sensible' (English) would be 'raisonnable'.

questions.q: What does 'On peut compter sur lui' mean?
questions.explain: 'Compter sur' means 'to rely/count on', so 'On peut compter sur lui' = 'You can rely on him'.

questions.q: What does 'assister à un concert' mean?
questions.explain: False friend: 'assister à' means 'to attend', not 'to assist'. 'To help' is 'aider'.

questions.q: What does « un jeu de société » mean?
questions.explain: « Un jeu de société » means a board game (literally a game of company), not a society.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'My parents are divorced'?
questions.explain: 'Divorcé' = divorced; 'marié' = married and 'fiancé' = engaged are near-miss distractors.

questions.q: What does 'faire de la randonnée' mean?
questions.explain: 'La randonnée' is 'hiking/rambling', so 'faire de la randonnée' = 'to go hiking'.
« Ma belle-mère » means stepmother or mother-in-law (not literally beautiful mother).
« Bricoler » means to do DIY or tinker with things; « le bricolage » is DIY.
False friend: « la lecture » means reading (the activity), not a lecture (which is « une conférence/un cours »).
